svg.text: Flywheel next — dispatch: four jobs, one host kind on three runners, the channels in and out, and the placements as a ladder the machinery offers

presenter · capture endpoint · triage · interpreter — the browser model is the interpreter alone · one binary on a laptop, in a pane, in a container · nothing addresses dispatch, it reads · capture never passes through it · the next rung is a decision on the status view
1 · THE FOUR JOBS · every job reads and writes only through the tools (193) · the data plane names none of them (216) · three are machinery given a host, the fourth is a session like any other

THE BROWSER MODEL = this job and nothing else (216a)
presents no sink · captures only through the capture tool (19) · reads no capture

three rules: only two jobs need a model, and both are bounded · only one job needs a long-lived process, and only under a socket chat · the browser model is the interpreter and nothing else — no context is carried between requests, nothing is compacted (7, 136)
2 · ONE HOST KIND, THREE RUNNERS · dispatch is a host (149, 217) · its two model jobs are sessions of A.7, started on a runner the sessions binding names (217b, 217c)
HOST · kind dispatcher · the same binary (217)
hosts.dispatcher: {name: dispatcher, bound: 0, kinds: [], presents: [chat]}
+ declares: the callers of its endpoint · the sources it triages · a runner per model job
flywheel dispatch is flywheel host with that declaration · joins by one command (205)
clones the state and the books under its root; no built repository — it names none
heartbeats as host/dispatcher · the tick every host runs: fetch · list · read · evaluate · effect (165)
lease only on a sink (148, 150) · never on an object · its declaration takes no work
stateless between ticks (217a)
the sink's mark, the capture keys, the signal files and the response files decide everything;
a restart reads the same state and reaches the same conclusion (7, 136)
a long-lived agent accumulates context and must compact; a host accumulates nothing
tool server · the binary's MCP server and its HTTP twin · every host serves it
an agent sharing the process calls it in-process or over stdio; a managed session calls
it over HTTP with the identity start_session issued, which the server checks (197)
listens on the private network only (155, 191); a platform whose sandbox cannot join
that network cannot run a managed session; the manifest is refused when it names one
publishing it beyond the private network is the operator's recorded choice (46)

a session record and a thread

across the operator's private network only (46, 191)
3 · CHANNELS · the machinery writes state and dispatch reads it · dispatch reaches the operator only as the bot · triage runs on the dispatcher's own tick · capture is decentralized (217d–h)
MACHINERY → DISPATCH · nothing addresses it (197)
state repository
the shared line
dispatcher · /hook
one route in both profiles
notify · a webhook
bounded fetch · 30s
notify · git-only: the git host's push webhook when the shared line moves (166)
notify · tracker: the App's issues, issue_comment, projects_v2_item webhooks (C.1)
fetch · git ls-remote every 30s and a fetch before every tick (165) · issues?since=<mark>
a notification only shortens the wait (130); never notified, it still converges by reading
no host, session or loop addresses dispatch (197, 217d) · the machinery writes state
sink.due: a register entry newer than the sink's mark · the cadence fired · the operator asked
"new decisions" is a notification kind routed to sinks like any other (82)
down: any host serves the page; back, it posts what is past the mark once (217f)

rich controls as the platform provides them; the numbered grammar beside them (155, 194)

the lease expires by the stated rule, never by racing (150); back, it reads that it lost it
down: replies wait in the chat and are applied once by delivery id when the presenter returns (217f)
TRIAGE CADENCE · the dispatcher's own tick rules (217e)
a capture with material to read and no signals charges a reader
immediate, subject to the bound · reads capture.signals_present false, the pointer present
at most triage.bound readers at once · default 1
reads the dispatcher's session records in a live state (32)
a forwarded single message charges no reader · always
the endpoint wrote its one signal (S21)
triage.cadence batches readers when the operator prefers a quiet hour · default none
reads flywheel.yaml triage.cadence, declared in the manifest beside curation's
triage is not curation (217e)
curation clusters unmoved signals against claims on its cadence or threshold (110)
and runs on a host with the machinery role; dispatch does not run it
curation's threshold counts unmoved signals; triage's bound counts running readers
a reader that stalls is a stalled session and takes the machinery's retry rule (65, 70)

each column is one piece of code shipped once — an adapter, a sign-in kind, a router kind, a runner — and which of them an organization uses is data in the manifest (139, 119) · no tier changes a machine, an atom or a profile operation (217j)

audit: history (167); plus the App's log; exported to the organization's log — every response is recorded with who gave it and when (153) at every tier · a tier's next rung is the same offer as a placement's
THE LADDER · the next rung is an offer
moving up a placement or a tier is a chore the machinery offers (123, 217k)
upgrade offer · a decision on the status view (141)
names the next placement or tier and what it needs;
answerable by control and number like every decision (152)
yes → the install effects (217k, 204)
the placement's own step — a process, a pane, a container, a
platform session — an effect with a proof, repeatable, never by hand
flywheel init records that the dispatcher exists and where it is placed
missing secrets · decisions under attention (207, 149)
bot token · App key or push credential · model key · inbound secrets
placed by the operator, never an agent; never a key that reaches a host
the rung is not climbed until each is placed
upgrading dispatch = the binary on its placement (208)
an older binary than the manifest's stamped version shows on the status view;
a down dispatcher is a stale host there, visible from the phone (141)
what ships first
the browser interpreter and the local dispatcher — the binary already specified;
then the container on flywheel-cloud, already the router the host binding names;
AgentCore and managed agents as triage runners when an org already runs there

dispatch is four jobs and no more, and the browser model is the interpreter alone (216, 216a) · it is a host whose declaration takes no work and presents the chat, stateless between ticks, its model jobs bounded sessions on a runner the engine cannot tell apart (217, 217a–c)

nothing addresses dispatch: it reads state through notify and a bounded fetch and reaches the operator only as the bot (217d) · triage is not curation (217e) · nothing is lost while it is down (217f) · capture is decentralized and the pointer must be reachable (217g, 217h)

three placements, one declaration; what differs is placement, secret store, route and model access (217i) · tiers are bindings (217j) · installed from the manifest, never by hand; the next rung is an offer, its secrets decisions under attention until placed (217k, 207)
